newsitem.title: ITALY: Isco sees Italy deficit/GDP ratio at 3.2 pct in 97.
newsitem.headline: Isco sees Italy deficit/GDP ratio at 3.2 pct in 97.

text.p: Italian public administration debt in 1996 will be 124 trillion lire, or 6.7 percent of gross domestic product (GDP), and fall to 63 trillion lire, or 3.2 percent, in 1997, state economic reasearch group Isco said.

Isco said in its latest report that its forecast was based on measures contained in the government's 1997 draft budget and had taken into account negative effects on public finances in the event that economic growth was less than expected.
It said a fall in the deficit would also result from cuts in official interest rates.

The public administration deficit is the parameter used by the Maastricht Treaty in its definition of criteria for early entry into European economic and monetary union (EMU), but the government's programmed deficit targets are based on public sector accounts.

On Monday, the Treasury said Italy's cumulative public sector borrowing requirement (PSBR) was 135.3 trillion lire at end-November 1996, about one trillion lire less than during the same period last year.

Isco said its debt forecasts "confirm that the process of correcting the imbalances in the Italian economy can continue and that the meeting of the necessary criteria for entry into European monetary union is possible, even if it isn't yet taken for granted."

Prime Minister Romano Prodi's 1997 budget aims to trim 62.5 trillion lire off the projected public sector deficit, but several economists have warned it will not be enough to bring down the deficit/GDP ratio to the 3.0-percent EMU parameter.
